Fig. 3
Natural and synthetic analogs of vitamin E (aT). As result of chemical synthesis, synthetic vitamin E products consist of all possible
combinations of R and S side-chain stereoisomers occurring at equal amounts (e.g., synthetic racemic vitamin E or all-rac-aT, formerly called dl-aT).
In the liver, aTTP recognizes preferentially RRR-aT and less also RSR, RRS and RSS-side chain isomers (the so-called 2R-aT-stereoisomers) for
enrichment in very low-density lipoproteins (VLDL), whereas the so-called 2S-aT-stereoisomers are metabolized and excreted.

Vitamin E metabolites
Broadly, two different types of vitamin E metabolites can be distinguished reﬂecting the mechanism by which they are generated in
the body (enzymatically and oxidatively) (Fig. 2). Enzymatically generated vitamin E metabolites are produced when their level
exceeds the capacity of aTTP to export them from the liver. For aT, which is selectively recognized by aTTP and speciﬁcally sorted
